newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles Council gives tentative OK to arena.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles Council gives tentative OK to arena.

text.p: The Los Angeles City Council on Wednesday approved a proposal to build a sports and entertainment complex in downtown Los Angeles and directed city attorneys to finalize the agreement, city officials said.
The city council approved the proposal by a vote of 13-2.
The vote capped months of negotiations over the development of the $250 million development for the Los Angeles Kings hockey team and the Lakers basketball team.
City negotiators said the basic framework of the deal was now in place, adding that the transaction would bolster the local economy by creating jobs.
A final City Council vote on the agreement could be scheduled before the end of the month, city officials said.
Earlier this week, the Council's ad hoc committee on the arena proposal approved the business plan.
Under the proposal, the city would contribute $70.5 million to the project.
The city's contribution would be funded with a taxable debt financing of $50.5 million and $20 million from a bond reserve fund, city negotiators said in a recent report.

The average annual cost of the city's contribution was estimated to be $6.8 million. This amount was expected to be fully recovered from tax revenues generated by the arena and from other sources, city negotiators said.
Critics of the plan said it put city taxpayers at risk.
